metadata.topic: The forward link reserved in 2026-06-23_ptsg-reset-command-bands (Hook E: Fmax via a one-clock-registered tick; master/slave sync via an externalized raw tick; Build Log #9 + future trace) was implemented in RTL as RH029 (pin-level prescaler_value input, tri0, 0 = PRESCALE parameter fallback, presc_valueM = value-1 registered off the compare path) and RH030 (presc_tick registered one-clock pulse; presc_cnt rollover on the raw tick; prescaler_match = raw pre-register tick) before any trace or spec text existed. The architect supplied the governing premise this session: the prescaler counter value is in principle not for external use; the prescaler only generates the base frequency. From that premise: the internal tick may be re-timed freely (Fmax), and only the tick is worth exporting (sync). The trace reads the RTL back into Layer 1 vocabulary, distinguishes the sync actually delivered (period-sharing: same value + common reset + C3-F21) from the sync the reservation described (tick-following slave: not built), identifies the C4-T2 form actually built (B-prime, pin-level value, neither pure A nor Chapter 5's bus-register B), and records as negative data six places where RTL, session record, and spec disagree (==/>= in presc_tickP — ruled in-session: == stays, fail-loud; zero-check timing; undriven prescaler_output; missing rst; header/tag narration lag; undefined live-write semantics).

metadata.intended_use: Structured for direct ingestion by a language-model context. A reader who loads this file plus ptsg_core.v (RH029/RH030) and Chapters 4/5 understands why the internal tick is registered, why prescaler_match is the raw tick one clock ahead of it, what 'slave' currently means (period-sharing, not tick-following), which C4-T2 form the reference implementation embodies, and which RTL details remain open.

decision_points.point: What the prescaler is: an observable counter, or a pure base-frequency generator?

alternatives.label: Observable counter
alternatives.characterization: prescaler_counter is a first-class output; Formations read the running value; its timing relative to the tick is part of the interface

alternatives.label: Pure base-frequency generator
alternatives.characterization: the counter is internal; only the tick has meaning outside; prescaler_counter is diagnostic/optional with no timing contract

decision_points.chosen: Pure base-frequency generator (architect's premise, this session).
decision_points.rationale: If the counter is not an interface, the internal tick may be re-timed without breaking any external contract, and the sync problem reduces to sharing the tick. Under the observable-counter reading, RH030's one-clock re-timing would silently alter an interface. The chosen reading is also what C3-F21 already assumed: a time-base a program cannot touch is not a counter a program reads. Chapter 5 § 5.10 already lists prescaler_counter as optional; this decision supplies the reason.

decision_points.point: Fmax: keep presc_tick combinational, or register it as a one-clock pulse (RH030)?

alternatives.label: Combinational presc_tick
alternatives.characterization: every FSM if(presc_tick) sees the 16-bit comparator plus the value mux on its path

alternatives.label: Registered presc_tick, one-clock pulse
alternatives.characterization: comparator cut at a flip-flop; FSM sees a clean FF output; +1 clock latency, +2 FFs

decision_points.rationale: All in-core consumers use presc_tick uniformly, so the whole tick grid shifts by exactly one clock and every interval (Stay, FG command, C4-F9 phase-lock) is preserved. This moves the comparator behind a register boundary rather than cancelling its delay; the rollover presc_cnt <= presc_tickP ? 0 : presc_cnt+1 keeps a short local comparator loop, acceptable. Regression anchor: RH028's terminal-value pattern (stay_cnt terminal = target-1) and the >= deadline must be re-confirmed under the shifted grid (Hook A).

decision_points.point: Sync: which tick is exported on prescaler_match — registered, raw, or both?

alternatives.label: Registered tick
alternatives.characterization: the same edge the core acts on; a slave registering it lands one clock behind the master

alternatives.label: Raw pre-register tick
alternatives.characterization: prescaler_match = presc_tickP; a slave that registers it once lands coincident with the master's internal tick

decision_points.chosen: Raw pre-register tick (RTL as built, RH030), matching the 2026-06-23 wording 'externalized raw (pre-register) tick'.
decision_points.rationale: The one-register delay is reproduced identically on both sides, so master and slave act on the same instant. Consequences to codify: prescaler_match leads the core's internal tick by exactly one clock; it is combinational (carries comparator delay) and must be registered by the consumer — a timing-analysed output, not a glitch-free strobe. 'Both' costs nothing at the Formation level if a registered copy is ever needed.

decision_points.point: What 'slave' means: period-sharing (delivered by RH029/RH030) versus tick-following (described by the 2026-06-23 reservation)

alternatives.label: Period-sharing slave
alternatives.characterization: all cores receive the same prescaler_value and one hardware reset; C3-F21 keeps them phase-locked forever; no tick input port — this is what RH029/RH030 provide

alternatives.label: Tick-following slave
alternatives.characterization: a core accepts an external tick in place of its own comparator (tick_in / bypass port), driven by the master's prescaler_match — not implemented

decision_points.chosen: OPEN — Tie candidate for Chapter 6. RH029/RH030 realise period-sharing; the reservation's rationale ('a slave follows an externally-supplied tick') describes tick-following.
decision_points.rationale: Period-sharing already yields deterministic, identical tick latency across cores (DP-2) and suffices for same-clock, same-reset compositions on one FPGA. Tick-following is needed only across clock domains or resets and adds a Core port — a Core-Formation-separation question the architect must rule on. Recorded so the reservation's promise and the RTL's delivery are not confused.

decision_points.point: Which C4-T2 form RH029 actually is

alternatives.label: (A) compile-time fixed
alternatives.characterization: parameter only, no pin — what the RTL header's Tie-lean line still says

alternatives.label: (B) runtime-configurable per Chapter 5 § 5.12
alternatives.characterization: Core-internal register written over the external-operation bus, no new pins — what the RTL tag says

alternatives.label: (B-prime) pin-level value input, as built
alternatives.characterization: prescaler_value is a tri0 input; 0/unconnected falls back to the PRESCALE parameter; the Formation decides whether the pin is a constant or a register; Chapter 5 § 5.2 already lists a prescaler_value input, mislabelled under option A

decision_points.chosen: OPEN — recommend recording B-prime as the reference implementation's form and updating § 5.2/§ 5.12; C4-T2 remains a Tie, only the contributor's lean and the reference form change.
decision_points.rationale: B-prime preserves Core minimalism (no bus decode, no reserved sub-opcode), keeps (A) as the zero-cost default through the fallback, and pushes the register-or-constant question to the Formation — the discipline-preserving extension pattern.

decision_points.point: Negative data: where RTL, session record, and spec still disagree (no ruling proposed)

alternatives.label: == vs >= in presc_tickP — RULED: stays ==
alternatives.characterization: the 2026-07-25 session record said '>= comparator protection'; the record was wrong, the file is right. Architect ruling 2026-08-27: a prescaler comparator that runs past its terminal is a fatal fault by concept; a loud 2^16-wrap is preferred to a quiet slightly-short period (fail-loud). Deliberate asymmetry with RH028, where >= on the stay counter serves the minimal-timing idiom; the time-base gets no such grace.

alternatives.label: Zero-check timing
alternatives.characterization: prescaler_value == 0 is tested on the raw input while presc_valueM is one clock behind; a 0<->non-0 transition yields one clock of mismatched compare target

alternatives.label: Reset hygiene
alternatives.characterization: presc_tick and presc_valueM sit in an always block without rst; one clock of X in simulation (the RH014 queued_opcode pattern)

alternatives.label: Narration lag
alternatives.characterization: header RH list ends at 028; Tie-lean line still says compile-time fixed; L579 tag reads RH030 with RH029's description; L458 '-cycle pulse' typo — third instance of the artifact ahead of the narration; L635 (presc_valueM <= prescaler_value - 1) is RH029 content under an RH030-only comment

alternatives.label: Live-write semantics undefined
alternatives.characterization: a new prescaler_value takes effect at the next compare as built; the stay counter has the barline rule, the prescaler has none

decision_points.chosen: Item 1 RULED in-session (== stays, fail-loud); items 2-6 recorded as OPEN, each the architect's call (Hook C, Hook D).
decision_points.rationale: Negative-data discipline: specification lag behind RTL truth is a recognised risk and is recorded openly with provenance rather than silently patched by the amanuensis.

themes.title: One decision, three fruits
themes.summary: No-prescaler-reset (C3-F21), the registered tick (Fmax), and the raw-tick export (sync) are one commitment — the prescaler is a sovereign time-base — seen from three sides. The premise 'the counter value is not for external use' is the hinge that makes the last two free.

themes.title: Period-sharing is not tick-following
themes.summary: RH029 gives every core the same period and, with a common reset, the same phase; it does not let a core follow another's tick. Both are 'master/slave'; only one is built. Naming the difference keeps Chapter 6 honest.

themes.title: The artifact ahead of the narration, again
themes.summary: The RTL delivered the reserved fruits before the trace existed; the header, the Tie lean, and one tag lagged. The discipline is unchanged: read the RTL back into the record, mark the gaps, do not let the record pretend it led.

key_outputs_for_repository: PREMISE (architect): the prescaler counter value is not, in principle, for external use; the prescaler generates the base frequency only. prescaler_counter is diagnostic/optional with no timing contract.

RH030 read-back: internal presc_tick is a one-clock registered pulse; the whole tick grid shifts by one clock uniformly; Fmax benefit = comparator behind a register boundary (not 'cancelled'); regression anchors unchanged pending Hook A.

RH030 read-back: prescaler_match = raw pre-register tick, leading the internal tick by exactly one clock; combinational, must be registered by the consumer; this is the 'externalized raw tick' of the 2026-06-23 reservation.

RH029 read-back: prescaler_value is a pin-level tri0 input; 0/unconnected = PRESCALE parameter fallback; presc_valueM = value-1 registered off the compare path. Form = B-prime (pin-level value), neither pure (A) nor Chapter 5's bus-register (B). C4-T2 remains a Tie.
Sync as delivered = period-sharing (same prescaler_value + common hardware reset + C3-F21); tick-following slave = not built, reserved for Chapter 6 (DP-4, Hook B).
RULED (architect): presc_tickP stays == — fail-loud; time-base overrun is fatal; deliberate asymmetry with RH028's >=.
OPEN (architect): zero-check timing; undriven prescaler_output; missing rst on presc_tick/presc_valueM; live-write semantics.

Narration corrections (architect-approved as canonical; entry dates 2026-07-16; not yet applied — source frozen during Layer 4 verification): RH029/RH030 header entries; C4-T2 lean line; L579 tag; L458 typo; two RH tags (RH030 presc_tick, RH029 presc_valueM) inside the tick always block (03_Sample_Implementations/.../RH029-030_header_patch.md).

closing_note: A metronome does not show you its gears. It gives you the beat, and the beat is all it promises. Once the prescaler was allowed to be only that — a beat, not a number to be read — two things became free at once: the beat could be handed through one more register on its way inside, costing a clock and buying speed; and the beat could be handed outside, raw, so that another core might take it in and, through its own single register, land on the same instant. The gears stay hidden; the beat is shared. What remains to decide is whether a second metronome may listen, or must only be wound to the same setting and started at the same moment. / メトロノームは歯車を見せない。拍を与える、それだけを約束する。プリスケーラがそれだけのもの——読み取る数ではなく拍——であることを許された瞬間、二つのことが同時に自由になった: 拍を内側へ渡す途中でレジスタを一段くぐらせ、1 クロックを払って速度を買うこと;そして拍を外へ、生のまま渡し、別のコアがそれを受け取って自身の一段のレジスタを通し、同じ瞬間に着地すること。歯車は隠れたまま、拍は共有される。残る決めごとは、二台目のメトロノームが聴くことを許されるのか、それとも同じ目盛りに合わせて同じ瞬間に始動させるだけなのか、である。
